recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-13948 unless a future terminology cleanup separately removes legacy RemittanceOutcome names from non-authoritative model or binding artifacts.
issue_request: FHIR-13948 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It asked to add an acknowledgement-style code to ExplanationOfBenefit.outcome because partial implied some adjudication had already occurred; the final resolution chose queued for a claim, preauthorization, or predetermination received but not yet processed.
initial_application: SVN-era commits cff1ea3a29 and fca077283d applied the issue by adding a received concept to remittance-outcome and then changing the relevant EOB, ClaimResponse, and remittance-outcome source to queued.
additional_context: The current build has active ExplanationOfBenefit and ClaimResponse resources. The old remittance-outcome source file was later refactored into the current claim-outcome source by 33b409a4b6 while preserving queued. A Zulip R4B RemittanceOutcome thread described a rogue legacy definition and recorded that it was fixed in source, supporting the current claim-outcome source as authoritative.
reconciliation: No source change was made because ExplanationOfBenefit.outcome currently includes queued in its short/comment and binds to ValueSet/claim-outcome, whose CodeSystem defines queued as received but processing not begun.

related_jiras.note: Earlier remittance outcome request for a pending/interim code; its resolution said partial covered pended adjudication but not the received-and-unprocessed state later addressed by FHIR-13948.
